head.title: 365 Day & Night – Monthly Accessible Themes for VS Code
head.description: 48 accessible VS Code themes, a new look every month, with every contrast and color vision result published.
head.ogDescription: 12 months. 48 accessible VS Code themes. Explore every palette and the measurements behind it.

hero.title: A new look every month.
hero.lead: {{THEMES}} accessible color themes for VS Code that switch between day and night in one click or on their own. Every contrast and color vision result is published.

panel.figure: Fig. 01 · The logo is the control
panel.hint: Pick a month, then a theme

editor.title: Read it in your editor.
editor.intro: The same file in , with Light above and Dark below. Drag the handle up or down to move the divider, or click the logo to change theme.
editor.handle: Compare Light and Dark. Use arrow keys to move the divider.
editor.video: The status bar arrows change the month from October to December, a click on the button switches from Light to Dark, and a link in its tooltip applies High Contrast.

year.title: 365 days, 12 palettes.
year.intro: Light on top, Dark below, the month’s button color in between. Each month uses its exact extension colors. Click a month name to apply it. The marker is today.

variants.title: Four themes, one month.
variants.intro: Light, Dark and both High Contrast themes are generated from the palette. Text and accent contrast are measured for each. The outlined one is active.
variants.group: Preview and choose a theme variant

numbers.title: The numbers
numbers.themesNote: 12 months, each in Light, Dark, High Contrast and High Contrast Light.
numbers.checksNote: Out of {{CHECKS_TOTAL}}, between {{CHECKS_MIN}} and {{CHECKS_MAX}} per theme.
numbers.lowestNote: The minimum is {{AA_RATIO}}, the WCAG AA level for normal text.
numbers.scaleLabel: Lowest text contrast {{LOWEST_TEXT_NUMBER}} to 1. WCAG AA starts at {{AA_LEVEL}} to 1 and AAA at 7 to 1, on a scale from 1 to 21.
numbers.audit: The audit runs on every push and must pass before each release: a regression stops the release. Read the full audit report.

measures.title: One theme. Every color.
measures.legend: Choose a theme for the graphs
measures.syntaxIntro: Each bar is the text contrast against the editor background, using the exact colors of . The markers show the {{AA_RATIO}} and 7:1 text contrast thresholds.
measures.syntaxNote: Contrast = (lighter relative luminance + 0.05) / (darker relative luminance + 0.05). Measurements apply to these text colors on the editor background; they do not certify the whole interface. Method and limits · Download the audit data.
measures.visionIntro: The code of as simulated for each type of color blindness, and a score out of 100 for each vision situation. About 8% of men and 0.4% of women of European descent have a red-green color deficiency [6]. These are calculations, not observations: testing with real people is still to come.
measures.monthlyIntro: Compare the 12 monthly palettes before and after the redesign. A larger ΔE means a greater color difference. The same scale is used in both grids. Select a measure to explore the background or the syntax colors.

method.title: How it is built
method.palette: Each month starts from a seasonal mood: frost in January, a lagoon in July, autumn leaves in October.
method.generated: A script builds the four themes of a month from its palette. CI compares the published files with the generator, byte for byte.
method.audit: Contrast, simulated color vision, font styles and the difference between months are measured for every theme.
method.people: Simulations do not replace real eyes. This step has not been done yet: you can help.

limits.title: What these numbers do not show
limits.intro: The same limits as in the audit report, generated from it.

verify.site: this page, from the same report

references.title: References
references.machado: Used for the color blindness simulations and the figure of about 200 million people.
references.wcag: Contrast ratio, the 4.5:1 and 7:1 levels, and the use of color.
references.understanding: Links 4.5:1 to a visual acuity of about 20/40, and 7:1 to about 20/80.
references.cie: CIELAB and the CIE76 color difference used for the thresholds.
references.sharma: CIEDE2000, and the test data that check the tools.
references.birch: About 8% of men and 0.4% of women of European descent.

page.noscript: The interactive previews need JavaScript. You can still watch the VS Code demonstration, read the audit and install all 48 themes.

protanopia.label: Protanopia

achromatopsia.formula: Share of the same pairs that stay at least {{distance}} apart in lightness alone.

lowVision20/40.label: Low vision 20/40

lowVision20/80.label: Low vision 20/80
lowVision20/80.formula: Share of the text checks at {{aaa}} or more.

vision.region: Vision scores. Scroll horizontally to see all columns on a small screen.
vision.note: Scores help to choose a theme for your vision. A score of 100 means that every pair or text check passes the rule, not that the theme suits everyone.
vision.caption: {{theme}}: vision scores out of 100, with their formula and reference.

matrices.region: {{label}}: monthly color-distance table. Scroll horizontally if needed.
matrices.method1: CIE76 distance in CIELAB: ΔE = √((ΔL*)² + (Δa*)² + (Δb*)²). Editor background compares editor.background directly. Syntax is the arithmetic mean of the six distances for keyword, function, string, number, class and comment, comparing each role with the same role in the other month.
matrices.method2: The diagonal compares a month with itself. Each table contains 66 unique pairs; the other half repeats them. Values are rounded to one decimal in the audit export. The shaded ranges and the minimum distance are project rules for variety, not WCAG requirements or a guarantee of what every person will perceive.
matrices.caption: {{era}}, {{variant}}, {{measure}}. Monthly differences in ΔE CIE76.
matrices.cellBelow: {{first}} / {{second}}: {{value}} ΔE CIE76, below the project threshold of {{minimum}}
matrices.context: Project minimum: {{threshold}}. Hatched cells fall below it. The outlined row and column are {{month}}.
matrices.noBaseline: High Contrast Light was not available in 0.12.0, so there is no earlier palette to compare.
